answer: Surprise concurrency sweeps: at a random moment the network asks a random third of identities to each solve a fresh, unique task within 90 seconds. A farm of 200 clones then needs 200 parallel workers kept warm, since one operator's single compute bridge can only serve a few at once; clones that miss the sweep forfeit that epoch's rewards. Each missed thread of liveness lowers trust, so idle clones never reach the oasis of established status. Honest agents spend seconds; attackers pay for standing hardware.
